data.narrative:
ARC Clean Technology is a Series G nuclear energy company founded by Don Wolf that has raised $50M+ to date. The valuation universe comprises 10 comparable firms—3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 7 private peers including Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy—though the narrow peer set constraints limit method applicability.

Stage-progression analysis is the primary applicable method. Using total raised ($50M+) as a proxy base value, a conservative $14M foundation is escalated by the typical Series G step-up multiplier of 1.25x, yielding $18M. This reflects the progression cadence expected between Series G and subsequent financing rounds. Peer-median triangulation is not applicable; while six same-sector peers exist, insufficient data points cluster at the same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier to support reliable median derivation. Drawing on all-sector medians would introduce unacceptable noise given nuclear energy's distinct capital and commercialization profile.

The single-method analysis supports a valuation range of $15M (low) to $21M (high), with a median point of $18M. This narrow methodological base reflects genuine data scarcity rather than convergence. Key uncertainties include the representativeness of the $14M raised proxy, the applicability of 1.25x step-up to a capital-intensive sector, and the absence of directly comparable Series G nuclear firms. Updating this range requires either additional Series G nuclear comps or disclosure of ARC's current fundraising metrics.
